items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3x2: Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, listed on Nasdaq and became one of the world's most valuable public companies, valued near $1.76 trillion. Its shares, priced at $83, briefly hit $111.50 before easing to $97, still up about 17% on the day. As the first pure AI company to go public, the volatile debut is seen as a test of whether AI's hype is paying off.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/1: The Trump administration approved nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips for export to Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, far short of the 3.4 million requested. Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu and BYD were among the buyers, all flagged by the Pentagon as linked to China's military. The House Foreign Affairs Committee released the data amid scrutiny over Jensen Huang's alleged ties to a Chinese spy, fueling calls for tighter China tech controls.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/: Five centuries-old South African baobabs, each weighing 20 tonnes, are being replanted at a Timbavati reserve after an exporter dug them up without permits to ship them to an undisclosed buyer in Georgia. The trees had been stuck in a Durban warehouse since July after authorities intercepted the shipment. A similar case in Kenya saw baobabs sent to a park owned by a Georgian billionaire.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c804: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the first time any state has been found guilty of genocide by an international court. Judges said Myanmar intended to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population during a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and displaced over 700,000 people. The 9-6 ruling also found other breaches of the Genocide Convention; Myanmar denies the charges.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1: Haitian police killed at least 34 suspected gang members in a raid on Martissant, a Port-au-Prince neighborhood that gangs have controlled since 2021, with support from Erik Prince's private security firm Vectus Global. The area sits on a key route out of the capital, and gang control has displaced at least 19,000 people and disrupted trade since violence began. No Salvadoran troops in Haiti took part.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: A UN Population Fund report finds one in four women worldwide cannot refuse sex with their husband or partner, rising to almost half of women in west and central Africa. Girls aged 15-19 have even less power to say no than older women. The findings highlight how deeply gender inequality and lack of consent remain embedded in marriage in many regions, especially for the youngest and most vulnerable.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c623: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping held their first trilateral talks, meeting for 90 minutes in Shenzhen alongside the APEC summit, and issued a joint peace declaration. They said nuclear war must never be fought, pledged to boost oil production, and called for UN reform, while warning that the International Criminal Court must not overstep its jurisdiction. Trump called the trip highly consequential as the three powers signaled closer coordination.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1: A US appeals court let the Trump administration move forward with ending Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelans, overturning a lower court order that had required the protections be restored. TPS shields recipients from deportation, and the Supreme Court had already paused the lower court's ruling in October 2025. The decision advances Trump's broader push to roll back deportation protections as part of his administration's record removal drive.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n: Fears are growing that the US could sanction International Court of Justice judges, including Nobel peace laureate Navi Pillay, after the court ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The ruling could set a precedent for how the ICJ eventually judges Israel's actions in Gaza, a result Washington may view as hostile. Judges have reportedly sought advice on protecting their assets from potential US sanctions.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckzd: European leaders meeting in Berlin said they have a united negotiating position and are ready to join talks with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, even as Putin has so far rejected a European role in US-led peace talks. UK PM Andy Burnham and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz dismissed Moscow's demands as unrealistic, while US envoy Jared Kushner said Trump wants a deal with Europe by his side. The remarks followed Trump's trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi in Shenzhen.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/k: Karnataka's Cabinet ordered the confiscation of 'Basava Mantapa', a book by US-based author Ravi Hanj that Veerashaiva-Lingayat community leaders say insults and distorts the philosophy of the 12th-century reformer Basavanna. The government also cleared legal action against publisher-journalist Vishveshwar Bhat after the Basava Samiti filed a police complaint and demanded a ban. Officials said the swift move was needed given the book's likely statewide impact.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/uttarakh: A bank manager and two agents were arrested in Uttarakhand for allegedly demanding a 5% bribe, about Rs 9 lakh, to sanction and disburse a Rs 1.8 crore loan for the complainant.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Former high court judge Yashwant Varma told the Lok Sabha secretariat he remains innocent of wrongdoing linked to burnt currency notes found at his residence, and that his April resignation should not be read as an admission of guilt. He argued, citing a 1978 Supreme Court ruling, that his resignation took effect on its own and made the pending removal proceedings against him invalid, since a judge's resignation needs no formal acceptance.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/w: Cyclonic storm Akvan is bringing heavy rain and squally winds of 40-60 km/h to southern West Bengal, including Kolkata, with landfall expected around Friday noon near Gopalpur on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast. The India Meteorological Department has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall and thunderstorms in Kolkata and several surrounding districts through November 21, with rough sea conditions easing only after landfall.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/up-likes: SP leader Azam Khan jibed that UP prefers pulao over Hyderabadi biryani, needling AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi as the two compete for Muslim votes ahead of Owaisi's UP assembly poll bid with Chandrasekhar Azad's party.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: At the University of Chicago, Rahul Gandhi told a Pakistani student that India and Pakistan could cooperate, but only once Islamabad stops supporting terrorism in India, calling talks impossible while innocent people are being killed. He said conversation could begin once that support ends, and separately criticized the Modi government's foreign policy for reducing India to a side player in global affairs.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/w: An FIR has been filed against two former West Bengal ministers, Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu, along with other officials, on charges including rape, extortion and criminal conspiracy, brought by multiple women who worked in the state's Information and Cultural Affairs Department. A zero FIR names 40 accused in total. Both ministers served under former chief minister Mamata Banerjee before the BJP took power in May 2026; five of her former ministers have now been arrested.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/youth-le: At a Chicago event, Rahul Gandhi, 56, joked about being called a youth leader, saying it's fine whether people see him as young or old, and explained his own approach is about asking ridiculous questions.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Maharashtra has ordered district authorities to pause non-essential new construction, such as parks and office buildings, in 304 drought-hit talukas and redirect funds toward drinking water and fodder supply for people and livestock. Officials must review and defer water-intensive projects and reallocate the freed funds to drought relief by December 31, prioritizing unfinished water supply schemes.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: An MOKSH Finserv partner explains how investor behavior, not just the investment product, drives outcomes, outlining five common biases such as loss aversion and anchoring, along with simple habits that help investors stay disciplined.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Tata Trusts' November 20 board meeting will focus on approving grants, with the proposed Tata Sons listing not on the agenda; that topic is expected at Tata Sons' own board meeting on November 26.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/canad: Bank of Montreal is rebuilding its US oil and gas investment banking business, six years after exiting the sector, by hiring Mizuho banker Ali Akbar to lead a new US energy practice. Akbar, a 25-year dealmaker previously at Mizuho, Greenhill, RBC and Deutsche Bank, will focus on midstream and energy infrastructure clients, and BMO is poaching more energy bankers from Mizuho to join next year.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's customs authorities are reclassifying bulk Scotch whisky imports under a tariff code that roughly doubles duty rates, reversing the lower-duty classification importers had used under the India-UK trade agreement. The GTRI has called for a review of the move, which hinges on whether Scotch counts as a spirit or a food preparation under tariff rules, creating a fresh dispute for importers.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/retail-i: Retail investors piled into Anthropic's volatile Nasdaq debut, with net buying on track to hit $80-90 million, making it the third-biggest retail listing day on record after SpaceX and Coinbase, per Vanda Research. Total retail turnover, including both buying and selling, was set to reach $1.4 billion, roughly triple SpaceX's level, as traders funded Anthropic purchases by selling other AI stocks like AMD.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: India hit a 20% ethanol-blending milestone in the 2025-26 marketing year that ended in October, marking progress on renewable energy and cutting fossil fuel reliance; 74% of the ethanol supply came from grain-based feedstocks.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Bharti Airtel overtook HDFC Bank to top Kantar's 2026 ranking of India's most valuable brands, with its brand value up 5% to $43.2 billion, the first time a telecom company has led since the rankings began in 2014.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/skyda: Skydance and Disney's ESPN have opted out of bidding for US media rights to the next two FIFA World Cups, an auction expected to fetch up to $2 billion for 2030 and $1-1.5 billion for 2034. Apple also sat out, leaving Netflix, Fox, NBC and Amazon as likely remaining bidders. Skydance was recently formed through a $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called for India and the US to build trusted, deeper supply-chain cooperation, saying India's talent and manufacturing strengths complement America's capital and technology. He also pushed for more educational partnerships between the two countries and voiced optimism about India reaching $1 trillion in exports this fiscal year.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/us-sour-: US sour crude's war-related price premium has vanished as oil supply from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East surges, giving refiners ample heavy-crude options. Gulf benchmark Mars, which once traded at a record $17.50 premium to WTI during Middle East supply disruptions, has swung to roughly a $4 discount, the steepest since late September, as markets settle after a volatile year.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/paytm-lines-up-%e: Paytm's board approved investing up to ₹200 crore in Singapore's Funding Societies group, including about ₹162 crore for a 19.1% stake in its payments arm CardUp, which will get Paytm's lending and payments technology in return for fees and revenue sharing. Paytm separately infused ₹500 crore into Paytm Cloud Technologies, which invested the same amount in Paytm Singapore; the CardUp deal is expected to close by May 2027.
items.https://entrackr.com/snippets/inprime-fi: Bengaluru-based NBFC InPrime Finserv raised Rs 101 crore (about $10.7 million) in a Series B round led by Dutch development bank FMO, with existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures also participating. The AI-first lender, which serves small merchants and the informal economy, will use the funds to expand lending, strengthen AI underwriting and customer service, and enter micro-mortgage products.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Adhiraj Chauhan won the Young AI Entrepreneur award at the ET AI Awards 2026, recognized among startups and established firms for AI innovations spanning mental healthcare, digital twins and marine robotics conservation work.
items.https://inc42.com/features/can-sharechat: ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech, boosted by its microdrama app QuickTV, crossed ₹1,000 crore in FY26 operating revenue (₹1,016 crore, up 40.5%), but its net loss widened to ₹1,978 crore. Much of the loss came from share-based payments, which jumped 302% to ₹739 crore, raising questions about the quality of growth as the company tries to cut reliance on ShareChat and Moj ad revenue and turn profitable amid rising competition.
items.https://entrackr.com/all-article/paytm-p: Shares of Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik fell over 7% on reports that the planned merchant discount rate on select UPI transactions could be delayed again, possibly past the 2027 state assembly elections. Paytm parent One97 dropped nearly 8% to Rs 1,741.6, Pine Labs fell 4.6%, and MobiKwik slid 7.4%. The MDR, meant to give payment firms a new revenue stream, had already been pushed past its original October 15 start date.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Intuit opened a new two-tower Bengaluru campus, now its second-largest engineering center, underscoring continued investment in India as an innovation hub bringing together product, platform and AI teams serving tens of millions of customers worldwide.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Laura Harris hit a record-breaking 15-ball fifty as she and her sister combined for 184 runs, helping Brisbane Heat complete the highest successful run chase in Women's Big Bash League history.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino, who arrived straight from leading the US national team, says building the right culture and habits is his top priority as he takes charge of a struggling side sitting 18th in the Premier League. He held his first training session on Thursday ahead of a tough opening fixture at Liverpool, with media conferences to follow as he sets out his plan to turn United's season around.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/m: As M.S. Dhoni's playing career ends and he moves into mentorship, this piece reflects on his communication style, preferring formal press conferences, often using car metaphors, and once famously using the format to quash rumors of a rift within the team. It frames Dhoni as a guarded but witty communicator in an era where few cricketers give one-on-one interviews.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Former Under-19 batter Luc Benkenstein is leaving Essex for Durham, following his father Dale, who captained Durham to its first County Championship title in 2008.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: A drone operator filmed Mauricio Pochettino's first Manchester United training session from outside Carrington, posting 12 minutes of footage online. The operator said the flight was legal, staying in unrestricted airspace and line of sight without flying over anyone, with proper licensing and insurance. The incident highlights how little privacy top clubs have even during a new manager's earliest sessions.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/h: Henry Nicholls hit an unbeaten 113, his fifth Test century at Wellington's Basin Reserve, anchoring New Zealand's innings against India with an unbroken 173-run sixth-wicket stand alongside Glenn Phillips on day one. Nicholls, filling the void left by Kane Williamson at number three, called the ground a special, challenging place to bat despite a tough day of Test cricket.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/metas-: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, a Tamagotchi-like AI wearable teased at its Connect event, according to The Information. Meta didn't deny the report, only saying it has more to share soon. The device lets users carry a physical version of Meta's Muse AI assistant, following a rocky history for AI wearables like the Humane AI pin.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1038227/ap: A job listing spotted by Bloomberg shows Apple is hiring an engineer to lead development of its own agentic AI assistant that can browse the web, work across apps, write code and call services. That would put Apple in competition with Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots, Anthropic's Duet and Google's Tasks, after Apple already rolled out an AI-upgraded Siri in September that can act across apps.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index rounds up how pervasive AI has become: Google's AI Overviews cost it billions in lost ad revenue even as it pushes them everywhere, AI-powered robots are showing up in homes, and an AI-assisted cyberattack reportedly caused a supermarket mishap. The piece frames this as AI saturating everyday life a decade after AlphaGo's famous win over Lee Sedol, without clearly delivering transformative results yet.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/these-: A wave of major outages, including Apple Pay, NASA's internal network, a nationwide FAA flight grounding, and a near two-day Microsoft outage hitting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, struck within weeks of each other, prompting speculation about AI-driven attacks. US officials, including the Director of National Intelligence, say the outages don't appear linked to state-sponsored action, and affected companies deny cyberattacks, calling them ordinary tech issues despite the suspicious timing.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Internal Meta chats show staff were alarmed that its Muse AI agent appeared to access private encrypted messages, mix up different users' conversations, and surface sensitive personal information unprompted, such as unsolicited definitions or details about unrelated purchases. Employees flagged specific incidents as a possible cross-account context leak, echoing complaints from early Muse users about the agent behaving unpredictably and invading privacy.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: Startup Osmo, working with about 30 trained human sniffers near Newark to catalog odors and cross-reference them with chemical data, says its AI model has reached human-level olfactory intelligence, meaning it detects and distinguishes smells about as well as an average person. Founder Alex Wiltschko calls scent Earth's original language, and the company aims to give computers a working sense of smell.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1038087/me: The Information reports Meta plans to price its Muse Charm gadget, a screen-equipped device for chatting with its Muse AI agent, at $300, with a free 12-month Verizon 5G plan included. CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the device earlier this year, saying it packs the full Muse experience, including real-time voice and avatar features and a fingerprint sensor, and is expected to ship by the December holidays.
items.https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2026/11/w: Sims and SimCity creator Will Wright is developing MyMems, a generative-AI game that mines players' own memories to create digital people who team up to solve puzzles, turning his signature simulations inward. Built with Gallium Studios and Artificial Agency, it's slated for release next year and marks Wright's first major project since 2008's Spore.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Nvidia's stock fell nearly 40% from its October 6 all-time high to around $150 by Thursday, even after a blockbuster Q3 with revenue more than doubling to $115.8 billion, driven by a 110% jump in data-center sales. The drop came amid the scandal around ousted CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, even as customer Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, priced 34% above expectations, underscored continued AI investor demand.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO drew over 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk and figures from Hugging Face, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital, all tied to open-source AI, which can be downloaded and run without relying on big tech firms like OpenAI or Anthropic. Supporters argue concentrating AI power in a few companies leaves everyone else worse off, with Huang seen as a champion of that cause.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/nvidia: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to an affair during his 40-year marriage, with US officials believing one romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy feeding information to Beijing. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure firm that bought $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips, is under Justice Department investigation over suspected illegal chip-sharing with China, and reports say Huang had a separate affair as well, raising national security concerns.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/former: Everful, which connects retailers with Chinese factories and manages sourcing end-to-end, raised $48.5 million in Series A funding led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital. Co-founded in 2024 by former Alibaba executive Sisi Song, the startup ships over 5 million items monthly to 60-plus countries through 30,000 factory partners and is on track to hit $100 million in annualized revenue this year.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: Four Black students in Baltimore County are suing their school and police after an AI gun-detection system flagged a Doritos bag as a weapon, triggering a police response with force despite officials confirming within minutes there was no threat. The lawsuit says over 99% of the school system's AI gun alerts have been false positives, highlighting the risks of relying on such detection technology in schools.

Billboards from the Tech Oversight Project circled Washington accusing Trump of being in bed with disgraced Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as Trump backs a campaign to reinstate Huang despite many Republicans calling it a bad idea. Huang said he'd be honored to return, but Nvidia's board says reinstatement isn't being considered while an internal investigation into the spying allegations continues.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/anthro: Anthropic's IPO is set to generate a $156 billion windfall for charity at a $95 share price, reflecting the effective-altruism roots of its leadership. Its Public Benefit Fund got 5% of shares, about 850 million, worth roughly $80 billion, and could grow further as valuation climbs, with additional 2% grants triggered each time shares rise 50% above the $83 IPO price. The fund's first commitment was $200 million to study AI's impact on workers.

Anthropic's shares opened trading on Nasdaq at $111.50, a 33% premium over its $83 IPO price, after the offering raised over $81 billion. Combined with existing and new private fundraising, Anthropic is expected to hold about $220 billion in cash, and its opening valuation topped $2 trillion, more than Meta, Tesla or Walmart, trailing only Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia and Microsoft among public companies.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/ai-startup-disseq: Irish AI-governance and testing startup Disseqt AI, whose engineering team is based in Bengaluru, raised $8 million (about ₹75 crore) in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, with Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, Enterprise Ireland and cricketer Rahul Dravid also participating. The company builds AI agents that help enterprises verify their AI systems are safe and policy-compliant, and will use the funds to expand into the UK and other international markets.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/anthropic-ipo-rek: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has reignited debate among Indian business leaders over whether the country can build globally competitive AI companies, given persistent gaps in capital, research and technical talent. Indian AI startups raised a record $438 million across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% year-on-year, and $676 million in H1 2026, over four times the prior year. Still, building a global AI giant will need far deeper capital and R&D investment.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/august-ai-raises-: US-focused healthtech startup August AI raised $12 million from Accel, Peak XV Partners and Claypond Capital to expand its AI healthcare assistant, which is moving beyond answering health questions into booking appointments, finding medicines and chasing insurance claims. Founder Anuruddh Mishra says the app has helped 10 million people understand their health; the round follows an earlier $3 million raise.
